workingTitle: A hot Jupiter has two sharply different atmospheric edges
coreFacts: The authors combined JWST NIRISS/SOSS and NIRSpec/G395H transit observations spanning 0.8 to 5.17 micrometres.
A wavelength-dependent shift in fitted mid-transit time carries information about differences between the planet's leading and trailing atmospheric limbs.

Injection-recovery tests found the new joint transmission and time-shift method reduced molecular-abundance mean squared error by about 30 to 50 times for H2O and CO relative to the next best tested approach.
WASP-94A b's morning limb is aerosol dominated, while its evening limb constrains H2O, CO2, CO, and tentatively H2S.
At 1 millibar, the evening and morning temperatures are 1177 +51/-46 K and 763 +35/-27 K, a difference of 415 +/- 58 K.
caveats: Morning-limb gas abundances remain unconstrained because high-altitude aerosols mask molecular absorption.
The composition synthesis assumes thermochemical equilibrium and uniform elemental enrichment.
Stellar flares, star spots, and faculae can also create time-dependent transit signals and must be excluded or modelled.
The framework assumes each limb has one thermal and chemical state during transit; rotating planets with stronger longitudinal variation may require more complex treatment.

sources.label: Mukherjee et al., accepted by The Astrophysical Journal Letters

sourceStatus: Primary peer-reviewed paper full text verified, including injection-recovery tests, observations, and discussion limits; separate corroboration is unnecessary for the paper's own measurements and validation tests.
